_about: Hand-written source for docs/reference/. Descriptions and examples are original and based only on PowerBridge's code, tests and observed runs. Regenerate the pages with: python -m pl_transpiler.tools.gen_reference

topics.title: Orders and exits
topics.intro: Words that place entries and exits. Order words are statements, so they have no return value. PowerBridge fills them in its own fill engine; see the usage guide (docs/USAGE.md) for the fill model.

topics.title: Position and entries
topics.intro: Read the state of the open position, its individual entries and recent positions. An index argument usually counts back: 0 is the current position or entry, 1 the one before.

topics.title: Strategy performance
topics.intro: Running totals over the closed trades of the strategy, updated as each trade closes.

topics.title: Bar and chart data
topics.intro: Facts about the bar being evaluated and the chart it belongs to. Several of these are fixed chart settings in PowerBridge rather than values computed from your data; each entry says so.

topics.title: Symbol properties
topics.intro: Properties of the traded instrument. PowerBridge takes them from the instrument config passed to the run (for example `get_config("NQ")`).

topics.title: Sessions
topics.intro: Trading-session times and days. PowerBridge does not read a session template from your data: most of these return fixed values that describe one session layout, so treat them as placeholders unless your data matches it.

topics.title: Dates and times
topics.intro: EasyLanguage has two date encodings. An EL date is a number like 1240102 (years since 1900, then month and day: 2 January 2024); an EL time is HHMM, or HHMMSS for the `_s` forms. A DateTime value counts days, with the time of day as the fraction.

topics.title: Math and lists
topics.intro: Numeric helpers. Results are rounded to float32 like MultiCharts. The trigonometric words work in degrees.

topics.title: Arrays
topics.intro: Helpers for arrays declared with `Array:` or `Arrays:`. The array is passed by name as the first argument; index ranges are inclusive.

topics.title: Drawing, colors and output
topics.intro: Chart objects, color constants and text output. A backtest has no chart, so PowerBridge accepts these calls but most have no visible effect; object-creating calls still return an ID.

Buy.desc: Opens or adds to a long position. Any open short is closed first, so a Buy while short reverses the position.
Buy.example: If Close > Open Then Buy ("LE") Next Bar At Market;

Sell.desc: Closes all or part of a long position. It never opens a short; use `SellShort` for that.
Sell.example: If MarketPosition = 1 and Close < Open Then Sell ("LX") Next Bar At Market;

SellShort.desc: Opens or adds to a short position, reversing any open long. `Sell Short` written as two words means the same.
SellShort.example: If Close < Open Then SellShort ("SE") Next Bar At Market;

BuyToCover.desc: Closes all or part of a short position without opening a long. `Buy To Cover` written as two words is the same order.
BuyToCover.example: If MarketPosition = -1 and Close > Open Then BuyToCover ("SX") Next Bar At Market;

Short.desc: Only meaningful as the second word of `Sell Short`. PowerBridge reads the two words as `SellShort`; `Short` alone is not an order.
Short.example: If Close < Open Then Sell Short ("SE") Next Bar At Market;

Cover.desc: Only meaningful as the last word of `Buy To Cover`. PowerBridge reads the phrase as `BuyToCover`; `Cover` alone is not an order.
Cover.example: If MarketPosition = -1 Then Buy To Cover ("SX") Next Bar At Market;

SetStopLoss.desc: Sets a protective stop for the open position, given as a money loss. PowerBridge always applies the amount to the whole position (the `SetStopPosition` mode).

SetProfitTarget.desc: Sets a profit target for the open position as a money amount; the position is closed once the open profit reaches it.
SetProfitTarget.example:
SetProfitTarget(1000);
If MarketPosition = 0 Then Buy Next Bar At Market;

SetBreakEven.desc: Once the open profit has reached the given money amount, places a stop at the entry price so the trade cannot turn into a loss.
SetBreakEven.example:
SetBreakEven(300);
If MarketPosition = 0 Then Buy Next Bar At Market;

SetDollarTrailing.desc: Trails a stop the given money amount behind the best open profit reached so far in the position.
SetDollarTrailing.example:
SetDollarTrailing(400);
If MarketPosition = 0 Then Buy Next Bar At Market;

SetPercentTrailing.desc: Takes two arguments: a profit threshold in money and a percentage. After the threshold is reached, the position is closed if it gives back that percentage of its peak profit.
SetPercentTrailing.example:
SetPercentTrailing(500, 30);
If MarketPosition = 0 Then Buy Next Bar At Market;

SetExitOnClose.desc: Closes any open position at the close of the last bar of each session.
SetExitOnClose.example:
SetExitOnClose;
If MarketPosition = 0 Then Buy Next Bar At Market;

SetStopContract.desc: Asks for the money amounts of the built-in exits to apply per contract instead of to the whole position. PowerBridge accepts it but does not yet honour it: its fill engine still applies the amounts to the whole position, so trades match `SetStopPosition`.

SetStopShare.desc: Equity-market spelling of `SetStopContract`. Like it, PowerBridge accepts it but still applies the exit amounts to the whole position.

SetStopPosition.desc: Makes the money amounts of the built-in exits (`SetStopLoss`, `SetProfitTarget` and the rest) apply to the whole position. This is the default.

SetStopLoss_pt.desc: Like `SetStopLoss`, but the distance is given in points (price units) from the entry price instead of in money.
SetStopLoss_pt.example:
SetStopLoss_pt(10);
If MarketPosition = 0 Then Buy Next Bar At Market;

SetProfitTarget_pt.desc: Like `SetProfitTarget`, with the target given in points from the entry price.
SetProfitTarget_pt.example:
SetProfitTarget_pt(20);
If MarketPosition = 0 Then Buy Next Bar At Market;

SetBreakEven_pt.desc: Like `SetBreakEven`, with the trigger given in points of open profit per contract.
SetBreakEven_pt.example:
SetBreakEven_pt(5);
If MarketPosition = 0 Then Buy Next Bar At Market;

SetTrailingStop_pt.desc: A trailing stop measured in points: it follows the best price reached in the position at the given distance.
SetTrailingStop_pt.example:
SetTrailingStop_pt(8);
If MarketPosition = 0 Then Buy Next Bar At Market;

SetPercentTrailing_pt.desc: Like `SetPercentTrailing`, with the profit threshold given in points instead of money.
SetPercentTrailing_pt.example:
SetPercentTrailing_pt(10, 25);
If MarketPosition = 0 Then Buy Next Bar At Market;

SameExitFromOneEntryOnce.desc: A strategy setting that limits how often one named exit may fire against the same entry. PowerBridge's runtime does not implement it; a run that reaches it stops with an error.

IntraBarOrderGeneration.desc: Strategy setting for evaluating orders inside a bar rather than once at its close. PowerBridge evaluates once per bar and does not implement this setting; a run that reads it stops with an error.

MarketPosition.desc: Direction of the open position: 1 when long, -1 when short, 0 when flat.
MarketPosition.example: If MarketPosition = 0 and Close > Close[1] Then Buy Next Bar At Market;

AvgEntryPrice.desc: Average fill price of the entries that make up the open position; 0 when flat.

entrydate.desc: EL date on which the current position was entered; 0 before the first entry.

entrytime.desc: EL time (HHMM) of the bar on which the current position was entered.

entrydatetime.desc: Entry date and time of the current position as one DateTime value. On PowerBridge's sample run it stayed 0, so do not rely on it yet.

ExitDate.desc: EL date on which the position the given number of positions ago was closed. `ExitDate(1)` is the most recent closed position.

ExitTime.desc: EL time (HHMM) at which the position the given number of positions ago was closed.

ExitDateTime.desc: Exit date and time of an earlier position as one DateTime value, indexed like `ExitDate`.

ExitPrice.desc: Price at which an earlier position was closed, indexed like `ExitDate`.

ExitName.desc: Name (the label in parentheses) of the exit order that closed an earlier position. Write it with its index, for example `ExitName(1)`; PowerBridge rejects the bare word.

barssinceexit.desc: How many bars ago the given earlier position was closed.

currententries.desc: Number of entries that are part of the open position.

currentshares.desc: Size of the open position in shares or contracts.

OpenEntriesCount.desc: Number of entries currently open in the position. Several entries build up when the strategy adds to a position.
OpenEntriesCount.example: If OpenEntriesCount < 2 and Close > Open Then Buy Next Bar At Market;

OpenEntryContracts.desc: Contracts held by one open entry, chosen by its index among the open entries.

OpenEntryDate.desc: EL date of one open entry, chosen by index.

OpenEntryTime.desc: EL time of one open entry, chosen by index.

OpenEntryPrice.desc: Fill price of one open entry, chosen by index.

OpenEntryProfit.desc: Open profit of one open entry, in money, chosen by index.

OpenEntryProfitPerContract.desc: Open profit of one open entry divided by its contracts.

OpenEntryMaxProfit.desc: Best open profit one open entry has reached so far.

OpenEntryMaxProfitPerContract.desc: Best open profit of one open entry, per contract.

OpenEntryMinProfit.desc: Worst open profit (largest open loss) one open entry has reached so far.

OpenEntryMinProfitPerContract.desc: Worst open profit of one open entry, per contract.

OpenPositionProfit.desc: Unrealised profit of the open position in money at the current bar's close; 0 when flat.
OpenPositionProfit.example:
If MarketPosition = 0 Then Buy Next Bar At Market;
If OpenPositionProfit < -500 Then Sell Next Bar At Market;

PositionProfit.desc: Profit of a position chosen by how many positions ago it was; index 0 is the open one.

MaxPositionProfit.desc: Largest open profit reached during a position, chosen by how many positions ago it was.

MaxPositionLoss.desc: Largest open loss reached during a position, chosen by how many positions ago it was.

MaxContractProfit.desc: Largest open profit per contract reached during a position.

MaxContracts.desc: Largest number of contracts held at once during a position, chosen by how many positions ago it was.

MaxShares.desc: Share-market spelling of the largest size held at once during the current position.

MaxEntries.desc: Largest number of entries open at once during a position.

maxcontractsheld.desc: Largest position size, in contracts, the strategy has held at any time so far.

MaxPositionsAgo.desc: Position-history word that counts back over earlier positions. It returned 0 on every bar of PowerBridge's sample run, so check it on your own strategy before relying on it.

PosTradeCount.desc: Number of trades (entry and exit pairs) inside the position the given number of positions ago.

PosTradeEntryBar.desc: Bars ago that a trade inside an earlier position was entered. The first argument picks the position, the second the trade within it.

PosTradeEntryCategory.desc: Order category code of a trade's entry, indexed by position then trade.

PosTradeEntryDateTime.desc: Entry date and time of a trade, as a DateTime value, indexed by position then trade.

PosTradeEntryName.desc: Label of the entry order of a trade, indexed by position then trade.

PosTradeEntryPrice.desc: Entry price of a trade, indexed by position then trade.

PosTradeExitBar.desc: Bars ago that a trade inside an earlier position was closed, indexed by position then trade.

PosTradeExitCategory.desc: Order category code of a trade's exit, indexed by position then trade.

PosTradeExitDateTime.desc: Exit date and time of a trade, as a DateTime value, indexed by position then trade.

PosTradeExitName.desc: Label of the exit order of a trade, indexed by position then trade.

PosTradeExitPrice.desc: Exit price of a trade, indexed by position then trade.

PosTradeIsLong.desc: True when the selected trade was long, indexed by position then trade.

PosTradeIsOpen.desc: True while the selected trade has not been closed yet.

PosTradeProfit.desc: Profit in money of a trade, indexed by position then trade.

PosTradeSize.desc: Contracts in a trade, indexed by position then trade.

grossprofit.desc: Sum of the profits of all winning closed trades so far.
grossprofit.example:
Vars: PF(0);
If GrossLoss <> 0 Then PF = GrossProfit / -GrossLoss;

grossloss.desc: Sum of the losses of all losing closed trades so far, as a negative number or 0.

percentprofit.desc: Share of closed trades that were winners, as a percentage.

numwintrades.desc: Count of closed trades with a profit.

numlostrades.desc: Count of closed trades with a loss.

numeventrades.desc: Count of closed trades that ended exactly flat.

largestwintrade.desc: Profit of the best closed trade so far.

largestlostrade.desc: Loss of the worst closed trade so far.

maxconsecwinners.desc: Longest run of back-to-back winning trades.

maxconseclosers.desc: Longest run of back-to-back losing trades.

maxiddrawdown.desc: Deepest drop in equity so far, measured bar by bar and including open profit. It is 0 or negative.
maxiddrawdown.example:
If MarketPosition = 0 Then Buy Next Bar At Market;
If MaxIDDrawdown < -2000 Then Sell Next Bar At Market;

AvgBarsWinTrade.desc: Average number of bars a winning trade was held.

AvgBarsLosTrade.desc: Average number of bars a losing trade was held.

AvgBarsEvenTrade.desc: Average number of bars a break-even trade was held.

totalbarswintrades.desc: Total bars spent in winning trades.

totalbarslostrades.desc: Total bars spent in losing trades.

totalbarseventrades.desc: Total bars spent in break-even trades.

currentbar.desc: Number of the bar being evaluated, counting from 1 at the first bar the strategy runs on.

BarInterval.desc: Size of each bar in units of the chart's resolution, for example 1 on a 1-minute chart. PowerBridge returns 1.

bartype.desc: Numeric code for the chart resolution. PowerBridge returns the code for intraday bars (1).

bartype_ex.desc: Extended resolution code that tells minutes apart from seconds or hours. PowerBridge returns the minute code (2).

intervaltype.desc: Resolution code of the data series. PowerBridge returns the intraday code (1).

intervaltype_ex.desc: Extended resolution code. PowerBridge returns the minute code (2).

barstatus.desc: Whether the current tick opened, is inside, or closed the bar. A backtest only sees closed bars, and PowerBridge returns 0 on its sample run.

basedatanumber.desc: Number of the data series the strategy is applied to. PowerBridge runs on one series, so this is 1.

currentdatanumber.desc: Number of the data series currently being calculated. Always 1 in PowerBridge's single-series runs.

maxbarsback.desc: The study's maximum-bars-back setting. PowerBridge returns a fixed 50; it does not reflect the `max_bars_back` argument of `run_el`.

maxbarsforward.desc: Chart setting for how many empty bars are shown after the last bar. PowerBridge returns a fixed 16.

tickid.desc: Identifier of the latest tick, used in real-time trading. It is 0 on historical bars, and PowerBridge always returns 0.

execoffset.desc: Real-time execution offset. On historical bars it is 0, which is what PowerBridge returns.

time_s.desc: Closing time of the current bar with seconds, as HHMMSS.

datetime.desc: Date and time of the current bar as one number. In PowerBridge the date part is the calendar date written as YYYYMMDD, the form the `...FromDateTime` words read.

dailyopen.desc: Daily open price for the bar's day. On PowerBridge's sample run it returned 0, so check it on your data before relying on it.

dailyhigh.desc: Daily high for the bar's day. Returned 0 on PowerBridge's sample run; check it on your data.

dailylow.desc: Daily low for the bar's day. Returned 0 on PowerBridge's sample run; check it on your data.

dailyclose.desc: Daily close for the bar's day. Returned 0 on PowerBridge's sample run; check it on your data.

tradedate.desc: Date of the last trade in real-time data. Without a live feed PowerBridge returns a placeholder, so do not use it in backtest logic.

tradetime.desc: Time of the last trade in real-time data; 0 in PowerBridge backtests.

tradevolume.desc: Size of the last trade in real-time data; 0 in PowerBridge backtests.

symbol.desc: Symbol of the instrument as a string, taken from the instrument config.

symbolname.desc: Name of the instrument's symbol as a string; same value as `Symbol` in PowerBridge.

description.desc: Long human-readable name of the instrument, from the instrument config.

category.desc: Numeric asset-class code of the instrument. PowerBridge returns 0.

bigpointvalue.desc: Money value of a one-point price move for one contract, from the instrument config (20 for NQ).

pointvalue.desc: Money value of the smallest price unit, which is `BigPointValue` divided by `PriceScale`.

pricescale.desc: How many price units make one point; for a quote with two decimals it is 100.

expirationdate.desc: Contract expiration as an EL date. PowerBridge returns a fixed placeholder date, not one from your data.

SymbolCurrencyCode.desc: Numeric code of the instrument's currency. PowerBridge returns 1.

Convert_Currency.desc: Converts an amount between currencies at a given date and time. PowerBridge's runtime does not implement it; a run that reaches it stops with an error.

sess1starttime.desc: Start time (HHMM) of the first session. PowerBridge returns a fixed 830.

sess1endtime.desc: End time of the first session. PowerBridge returns a fixed 1515.

sess1firstbartime.desc: Closing time of the first bar of the first session. PowerBridge returns a fixed 831.

sess2starttime.desc: Start time of the second session. PowerBridge models one session and returns the first session's 830.

sess2endtime.desc: End time of the second session; PowerBridge returns the first session's 1515.

sess2firstbartime.desc: First-bar time of the second session; PowerBridge returns the first session's 831.

sessioncount.desc: Number of sessions in the weekly template. PowerBridge returns 5 (one per weekday).

sessioncountms.desc: Variant of `SessionCount` for the money-management session template; also 5 in PowerBridge.

SessionStartTime.desc: Start time of a session, given a session type and a session number. PowerBridge returns a fixed 1700.

SessionEndTime.desc: End time of a session, given a session type and a session number. PowerBridge returns a fixed 1600.

SessionStartDay.desc: Weekday (0 = Sunday) on which a session starts, given a session type and number. PowerBridge models sessions 1 to 5 as opening the evening before each weekday and returns 0 for other numbers.

sessionendday.desc: Weekday on which a session ends. PowerBridge returns 1 (Monday).

SessionStartTimeMS.desc: Start time of a session in the money-management template, by session number. PowerBridge returns 830.

SessionEndTimeMS.desc: End time of a session in the money-management template. PowerBridge returns 1515.

SessionStartDayMS.desc: Start weekday of a money-management session. PowerBridge returns 1.

sessionenddayms.desc: End weekday of a money-management session. PowerBridge returns 1.

sessionlastbar.desc: True on the last bar of a trading session. PowerBridge decides this from the bar dates: the bar is last when the next bar falls on a new day.
sessionlastbar.example: If SessionLastBar and MarketPosition <> 0 Then Sell Next Bar At Market;

CurrentDate.desc: Today's date as an EL date. In a PowerBridge backtest it follows the bar being evaluated, so results do not depend on when you run them.

CurrentTime.desc: Current time as HHMM. In a PowerBridge backtest it follows the bar being evaluated.

CurrentTime_s.desc: Current time as HHMMSS. Unlike `CurrentTime`, PowerBridge does not tie this one to the bar, so treat it as a clock reading.

LastCalcDateTime.desc: When the study was last calculated, as a DateTime value. Read from a clock, not from the bars.

LastCalcJDate.desc: Date of the last calculation as a whole day count (the DateTime day number).

LastCalcMMTime.desc: Time of the last calculation in minutes since midnight.

LastCalcSSTime.desc: Time of the last calculation in seconds since midnight.

LastCalcmSTime.desc: Time of the last calculation in milliseconds since midnight.

Year.desc: Year part of an EL date, as years since 1900 (2024 gives 124).

Month.desc: Month (1 to 12) of an EL date.
Month.example: If Month(Date) = 12 and MarketPosition <> 0 Then Sell Next Bar At Market;

DayOfMonth.desc: Day of the month (1 to 31) of an EL date.

DayOfWeek.desc: Weekday of an EL date, with Sunday as 0 and Saturday as 6.
DayOfWeek.example: If DayOfWeek(Date) = 5 and MarketPosition <> 0 Then Sell Next Bar At Market;

DateToJulian.desc: Turns an EL date into a day count (the date part of a DateTime value).

JulianToDate.desc: Turns a day count back into an EL date; the reverse of `DateToJulian`.

ELDateToDateTime.desc: Turns an EL date into a DateTime day count with no time part.

ELTimeToDateTime.desc: Turns an HHMM time into the matching fraction of a day, so it can be added to a DateTime date.

ELTimeToDateTime_s.desc: Turns an HHMMSS time into the matching fraction of a day.

DateTime2ELTime.desc: Takes the time of day from a DateTime value and returns it as HHMM.

DateTime2ELTime_s.desc: Takes the time of day from a DateTime value and returns it as HHMMSS.

Time2Time_s.desc: Turns HHMM into HHMMSS by adding zero seconds (1015 becomes 101500).

Time_s2Time.desc: Turns HHMMSS into HHMM, dropping the seconds.

EncodeDate.desc: Builds a DateTime day count from year, month and day. A two-digit year below 50 is read as 20xx, otherwise 19xx.

EncodeTime.desc: Builds a fraction of a day from hours, minutes, seconds and milliseconds.

IncMonth.desc: Adds a number of months to a DateTime value. The day of the month is kept, so 31 January plus one month rolls over into early March.

DateToString.desc: Formats the date part of a DateTime value as text. PowerBridge uses a day/month/year layout such as `2/01/2024`.

TimeToString.desc: Formats the time part of a DateTime value as text with seconds and AM/PM, such as `9:30:00 AM`.

DateTimeToString.desc: Formats a DateTime value as date and time text, in the same layouts as `DateToString` and `TimeToString`.

DateTimeToString_Ms.desc: Like `DateTimeToString`, with a 24-hour clock and milliseconds.

FormatDate.desc: Formats a DateTime value with a pattern string such as `"yyyy-MM-dd"`. The pattern comes first.

FormatTime.desc: Formats the time part of a DateTime value with a pattern string such as `"HH:mm"`.
FormatTime.example:
Vars: S("");
S = FormatTime("HH:mm", ELDateToDateTime(Date) + ELTimeToDateTime(Time));

StringToDate.desc: Reads a month/day/year text date and returns its DateTime day count.

StringToTime.desc: Reads a time of day such as `"09:30:00 AM"` and returns it as a fraction of a day.

StringToDateTime.desc: Reads a month/day/year date followed by a time and returns one DateTime value.

StringToDTFormatted.desc: Reads a date (and optionally time) using a pattern you give as the second argument.

YearFromDateTime.desc: Year of a DateTime value. PowerBridge expects the date part written as YYYYMMDD, which is what its `DateTime` word gives.

MonthFromDateTime.desc: Month of a DateTime value (date part as YYYYMMDD in PowerBridge).

DayFromDateTime.desc: Day of the month of a DateTime value (date part as YYYYMMDD in PowerBridge).

DayOfWeekFromDateTime.desc: Weekday of a DateTime value, Sunday = 0 (date part as YYYYMMDD in PowerBridge).

HoursFromDateTime.desc: Hour (0 to 23) of the time part of a DateTime value.

MinutesFromDateTime.desc: Minute (0 to 59) of the time part of a DateTime value.

SecondsFromDateTime.desc: Second (0 to 59) of the time part of a DateTime value.

MilliSecondsFromDateTime.desc: Millisecond (0 to 999) of the time part of a DateTime value.

AbsValue.desc: Absolute value: the number without its sign.

Sign.desc: Returns 1 for a positive number, -1 for a negative one and 0 for zero.

Power.desc: Raises the first argument to the power of the second.

ExpValue.desc: e raised to the given power; the reverse of `Log`.

Round.desc: Rounds the first argument to the number of decimals given by the second. The result is a float32, so it may print as a close neighbour such as 2.3499999.

IntPortion.desc: Whole-number part of a value, cutting toward zero (-2.75 gives -2).

FracPortion.desc: Fractional part of a value, keeping its sign (-2.75 gives -0.75).

Floor.desc: Largest whole number not above the value (-2.5 gives -3).

Ceiling.desc: Smallest whole number not below the value (-2.5 gives -2).

Sine.desc: Sine of an angle given in degrees.

Cosine.desc: Cosine of an angle given in degrees.

Tangent.desc: Tangent of an angle given in degrees.

Cotangent.desc: Cotangent (one over the tangent) of an angle given in degrees.

ArcTangent.desc: Inverse tangent, returned in degrees (1 gives 45).

Random.desc: A random number below the given limit. PowerBridge's runtime does not implement it; a run that reaches it stops with an error.

MaxList.desc: Largest of the values passed in. Takes any number of arguments.
MaxList.example:
Vars: Top(0);
Top = MaxList(Open, Close, High[1]);

MinList.desc: Smallest of the values passed in. Takes any number of arguments.

MaxList2.desc: Second-largest of the values passed in.

MinList2.desc: Second-smallest of the values passed in.

NthMaxList.desc: The first argument N picks the N-th largest of the remaining values; 0 when N is out of range.
NthMaxList.example:
Vars: Second(0);
Second = NthMaxList(2, Close, Close[1], Close[2], Close[3]);

NthMinList.desc: The first argument N picks the N-th smallest of the remaining values.

SumList.desc: Sum of all values passed in.

AvgList.desc: Arithmetic mean of all values passed in.
AvgList.example:
Vars: Mid(0);
Mid = AvgList(High, Low, Close);

Crosses.desc: Used in `A crosses above B` or `A crosses below B`: true on the bar where A moves from one side of B to the other. It only works in that phrase. `crosses over` and `crosses under` are accepted as the same as `crosses above` and `crosses below`.

array_getmaxindex.desc: Highest index of a dynamic or fixed array (an array declared `A[4]` has indices 0 to 4).

array_setmaxindex.desc: Resizes an array so that its highest index is the given number. Returns true.

array_sum.desc: Sum of the elements from a start index to an end index, both included.

array_contains.desc: True when the value appears anywhere in the array.

array_indexof.desc: Index of the first element equal to the value, or -1 when there is none.

array_compare.desc: Compares a run of elements of two arrays: source array, source start, target array, target start, count. Returns 0 when equal, 1 when the first difference is larger in the source and -1 when smaller.

array_copy.desc: Copies a run of elements from one array into another (or within one array): source, source start, target, target start, count. Elements that would fall outside either array are skipped.

array_setvalrange.desc: Sets every element from a start index to an end index (both included) to one value.

array_sort.desc: Sorts the elements between two indexes in place: ascending when the last argument is true, descending when false.

array_gettype.desc: Code for the array's element type: 2 for true/false, 3 for text, 7 for numbers.

array_getfloatvalue.desc: Reads a numeric element by index; an out-of-range index gives 0.

array_getintegervalue.desc: Reads an element by index as a whole-number value.

array_getbooleanvalue.desc: Reads a true/false element by index.

array_getstringvalue.desc: Reads a text element by index; an out-of-range index gives an empty string.

array_setfloatvalue.desc: Writes a numeric value into an element: array, index, value.

array_setintegervalue.desc: Writes a whole-number value into an element: array, index, value.

array_setbooleanvalue.desc: Writes a true/false value into an element: array, index, value.

array_setstringvalue.desc: Writes a text value into an element: array, index, value.

fill_array.desc: Sets every element of an array to one value, including every row of a multi-dimensional array.

ArraySize.desc: Array size query. PowerBridge's runtime does not implement it; use `Array_GetMaxIndex` instead. A run that reaches it stops with an error.

TL_New.desc: Draws a trend line between two points, each given as date, time (HHMM) and price, and returns the new line's ID.
TL_New.example:
Vars: ID(0);
If CurrentBar = 10 Then ID = TL_New(Date[5], Time[5], Low[5], Date, Time, Low);

TL_New_s.desc: Like `TL_New`, with times given as HHMMSS.

TL_GetValue.desc: Price of a trend line at a date and time. That interpolation is not measured against MultiCharts, so a run that reaches it stops with an error instead of returning 0.

TL_SetColor.desc: Sets a trend line's color: line ID, then a color value.

TL_SetStyle.desc: Sets a trend line's line style (solid, dashed and so on): line ID, then a style constant such as `Tool_Solid`.

TL_SetExtLeft.desc: Turns extending a trend line to the left on or off: line ID, then true or false.

TL_SetExtRight.desc: Turns extending a trend line to the right on or off: line ID, then true or false.

Tool_Solid.desc: Line-style constant for a solid line (1), used with `TL_SetStyle`. Measured on g-tool-001-dashed: Tool_Solid through Tool_Dashed3 are 1 through 5.

Arw_New.desc: Places an arrow at a date, time and price; the fourth argument is a true/false direction flag. Returns the arrow's ID.
Arw_New.example:
Vars: ID(0);
If Close > Close[1] Then ID = Arw_New(Date, Time, Low, false);

Arw_New_s.desc: Like `Arw_New`, with the time given as HHMMSS.

text_new.desc: Places a text label at a date, time and price and returns its ID.
text_new.example:
Vars: ID(0);
If CurrentBar = 1 Then ID = Text_New(Date, Time, High, "start");

text_new_s.desc: Like `Text_New`, with the time given as HHMMSS.

Commentary.desc: Writes text to the per-bar commentary window. Several arguments are joined with +. A #BeginCmtry block is not executed: PowerBridge has no commentary-on mode. The text does not change trades.

CommentaryCL.desc: Like Commentary, for the closing window. Several arguments are joined with + and the text does not change trades.

alertenabled.desc: True when alerts are switched on for the study. PowerBridge backtests run with alerts off, so it is false.

Red.example:
Vars: C(0);
If Close < Open Then C = Red Else C = Green;
